problem: The Work drawer lists each program by stage and stops there. A reader cannot see which epics and slices of a program are planned, in progress, or done. The reader opens each program in turn to learn where its work stands.
why_now: ADR-0047 made the tracker the one source of stage and status. The record index now holds the status of each epic and slice, and no surface shows it as a board.
approach: A Kanban board is a full page in the viewer shell, at the address #/board. The program board shows each program as a card in its stage column. A card opens the epic board of that program, with the epics in three status columns, and a switch shows the slices. Pure rule modules group, search, and sort the cards, and the address holds the view state. The index gains the epic title and a build time. A copy icon copies a start prompt. The board changes no workflow state, and the Work drawer stays.

alternatives.option: A lane matrix: one row for each program, and selected programs turn into columns
alternatives.rejected_because: The engineer compared the prototype and chose the two-level board. The stage showed only as a badge, and 26 rows made a long page.

alternatives.option: A stage board with a dock for selected programs
alternatives.rejected_because: Two regions share the width, and a fourth docked program needs a sideways scroll. The two-level board keeps the stage columns and drops the dock.

alternatives.option: A roster on the left and a board whose shape follows the selection
alternatives.rejected_because: The reader must learn three board shapes. The engineer liked the idea and preferred one shape for each level.

alternatives.option: Put the status columns inside the Work drawer
alternatives.rejected_because: ADR-0034 built this and rejected it. Columns behind a sideways scroll spend the width of the drawer, and each lane needs a second scrollbar.

alternatives.option: A second HTML entry with its own data file and a new tracker operation
alternatives.rejected_because: A second built file breaks the one-shell model and the byte check of the build. The index read already covers the new operation.

alternatives.option: A source field on each record, content hashes, and a log of each status change
alternatives.rejected_because: One reader on one machine does not need an audit. The log would be a second store of workflow state.

alternatives.option: One data file for each program, loaded when a card opens, with windowed columns
alternatives.rejected_because: The index holds 26 programs and 112 epics, so no scale problem exists. A page opened from disk cannot fetch a further file.

alternatives.option: Show the epic id in place of a title, and leave out slices with no program
alternatives.rejected_because: The epics of one program read alike without a title. A board that drops 42 slices shows totals that differ from the index.

alternatives.option: Copy the tracker command of the next step from a card
alternatives.rejected_because: The index holds no map from a stage to a command. The engineer chose a start prompt for the design and build workflows.

out_of_scope: A change of workflow state from the board, and drag and drop
The multi-selection of programs and vertical swim lanes, which the engineer removed on 2026-11-14
A sort by date, priority, or assignee, because the index holds none of them
A filter by epic status on the program board
A rule that closes an epic on its last slice, or a check of pull requests at a workflow start. The engineer handles that check outside this program
A change to the Work drawer
risks: A design named board would take the address of the board. The engineer accepted this risk
The build time changes the committed index on each build, so each build shows a diff
22 epics are open while all of their slices are done, because merged pull requests were not recorded. The board shows them as open until a person records the merge
The start prompt names a command of another plugin as text. A renamed command leaves a stale prompt on the board
testing: Rule tests: the stage column and counts of each program, each emitted status in its column, true totals, empty reasons, a hidden column, and the No program card
Sort tests: name, open, and progress, each with the name tie-break and a program with no epic
Codec tests: a round trip of each query key, an unknown key, an unknown program, and the No program board
Prompt tests: each stage and epic case, the merged-open case, and no icon on a finished record
Index tests: the epic title, built_at outside sources and the projector, and a viewer load of an index without both fields
Component tests: the card click, the back control, the slice switch, the Slices done mark, the copy notices, and the build time header
Shell tests: the Work drawer opens over the board, and a slice address marks its row on the epic page
A browser check at 1280 by 800: five stage columns with no sideways scroll of the page
reviewer_focus: Does the build time sit outside the sources block and outside the projector, so the stale check and the golden index still hold
Does any board file compute a status that the index does not hold
Does the amendment leave the rule of ADR-0034 true for the drawer
Is the reserved segment for the No program card safe against a real design name
unknowns: Whether the two new index fields need a schema version step, or stay optional fields
How the epic page marks one slice row. It has no anchor for a slice today
Whether the clipboard call works in each host that embeds the viewer, such as a published Artifact
